Separately, actual rigid constant branches or local finite pure closed curve images and normalization lifts for smooth strict boundaryless ground-field curve maps over arbitrary complete nontrivially valued fields. result.report:
Theorems A and C and Proposition B are established at their stated partial scope. I reconstructed the supplied n100 proof rather than treating its receipt, origin, or hash as an assumption. No substantive task-granted premise or previous verdict was used. The original classification remains open, as expressly permitted by the task.

For smooth recognition, the affinoid embedding has the required field, strictness, connectedness, normality, and dimension hypotheses. The supplied van der Put, Thuillier, and Berkovich bodies support an actual affinoid-domain embedding. The two boundary equalities then identify ordinary interiors; they do not identify the whole affinoid with an ordinary open. This works at every analytic point. Compact tests transport through that ordinary-open isomorphism and extend by zero legitimately. Wanner’s algebraic scalar tests are included among ordinary analytic CLD tests, and their integration agrees with canonical CLD integration. Equality of the entire test sheaves is unnecessary. Wanner’s comparison is applied only to an ordinary open of a smooth proper algebraic curve over the same algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field. Both signs therefore become subharmonic, and the two-sign criterion and locality give harmonicity.

The n100 reconstruction checks its supporting lemmas in every degree used. Reducedness supplies S1 by the given prime-avoidance argument. Closed-embedding test lifting uses actual quotient-sheaf lifts of unit germs and compact ordinary cutoffs. In the positive-current limit argument, the symmetric coefficient estimate has the correct CLD sign and the factor p! in Q^p; bounded coefficient-measure masses justify continuous multiplication. Scalar approximation is used only for this fixed-test estimate, never as differentiated-test convergence.

The reconstructed S1 Poincaré–Lelong argument uses CLD 14.7.2 only with target dimension one. Compact sources and their intersections retain S1 and the checked pure relative dimension. The calibrated product carries the actual zero-fibre multiplicities and standard primitive last-coordinate calibration. Green’s formula, boundary inclusion-exclusion, the negative inner-face contribution, the vanishing outer face, and the lower-dimensional side faces give the stated sign and divisor current. The rejected inference from one regular element to S1 is not used. Successive cuts operate on reduced effective component cycles, preserve the ambient equation through doubly closed positive smooth wedges, and retain their actual positive coefficients. They do not identify an arbitrary embedded-prime quotient with the constructed cycle.

Rigid-puncture removal is also established independently. Ordinary scalar germs at a rigid point are locally constant by the minimal-polynomial argument, including inseparable residue extensions. The radial cutoffs have compact supports shrinking to the puncture, zero total differentiated integral, and uniformly bounded variation with mass ℓ[H(a):K], using the full residue-field degree. Consequently a current supported at the puncture is an evaluation functional whose coefficient vanishes by continuity. No measure hypothesis on the continuous function’s Hessian is introduced. Component separation, puncture removal, and reassembly with the original curve’s own generic lengths prove intrinsic restriction, including nonreduced structures. The conductor argument supplies an actual normalization isomorphism locus with locally finite rigid exceptions; removability establishes the upstairs equation. The additional direct-image identity is checked against every compact ordinary top-degree test, independently of the upstairs equation.

Theorem A then uses normalization smoothness only over the perfect algebraically closed field. Harmonicity descends through the finite surjective normalization and reduction morphisms only after recognition. GR’s curve theorems supply the complete extension-field and curve-map quantifiers, G-local real PL regularity, and residual numerical triviality. No ordinary CLD smoothness or harmonic approximation is inferred.

For Proposition B, the constant branch factors the entire bounded Tate-algebra map through a finite field: completeness and spectral-norm equivalence justify limits of series in that field. In the other branch, the actual fibre over each rigid image’s completed residue field is a closed subspace of a scalar-extended finite Artinian zero algebra. Zariski upper semicontinuity and the strict Nullstellensatz eliminate positive-dimensional fibres at all analytic source points. Relative interior follows from the separated-target boundary equality, so the local finiteness criterion applies without assuming compactness of the original entire fibre. The subsequent strict affinoid construction, integral kernel image, dimension calculation, all-point analytic surjectivity through nonzero completed fibre algebras, and bounded finite normalization lift are valid over arbitrary complete nontrivially valued fields, including inseparable cases.

Theorem C uses the actual closed image inside the ordinary interior of its target affinoid. Intrinsic restriction and normalization transfer precede recognition and harmonic pullback on the actual source neighbourhood. Its conclusion concerns ground-field probes. Neither scalar-current ascent nor universal ambient classical pluriharmonicity follows or is claimed.

The optional generic-length associativity calculation and regular algebraic cover correction are valid in their stated settings. The latter uses a Zariski cover containing all scheme closed points and the Jacobson property, so it covers all analytification points without a rigid-point-density argument.

Harmless wording clarification: in Proposition B’s proof, replace “strict affinoid domain algebra” by “strict affinoid algebra that is an integral domain.” No mathematical repair is required. Thuillier and Berkovich were checked using the supplied original bodies; unsuccessful fresh PDF retrievals do not replace that evidence. The two BGR facts were independently corroborated in Bosch’s primary treatment. Compilation, hashes, and finite diagnostics play no role in this verdict. Passage quotations preserve source wording or mathematical notation, with whitespace and extracted glyphs normalized.

premises: For a k-affinoid algebra A, A is noetherian, all its ideals are closed, M(A)→Spec(A) is surjective, and its spectral seminorm vanishes exactly on nilpotents; when A is reduced, that seminorm is a norm equivalent to its structural Banach norm. A strict affinoid algebra has a bounded quotient presentation by a unit-radius Tate algebra. CLD 11.1.2.

Good analytic spaces have affinoid neighbourhood bases, and ordinary opens are analytic domains. Over a complete nontrivially valued field, every point of a good strict analytic space has a strict affinoid neighbourhood, also after restricting to a prescribed ordinary open. CLD 11.1.5–7 and 11.7.7.

Coherent ideals on M(A) correspond to ideals of A; their closed analytic subspaces are M(A/I), with quotient structure sheaf. Zariski closed sets are their carriers. Reduction preserves the ordinary and Zariski carriers. CLD 11.2.1–2.

Analytic domains preserve local analytic dimension. A strict affinoid’s dimension equals its algebra’s Krull dimension. Affinoids have finitely many irreducible components; irreducible analytic spaces are pure, and their proper Zariski closed subsets have smaller dimension. Components after domain restriction retain the dimensions of the original components. CLD 11.2.3–5.

Regularity and Serre’s S_j conditions persist under analytic-domain restriction. Analytic normalization is finite surjective and locally is the integral closure of the reduced affinoid algebra in its total quotient ring; normalization is local and commutes with analytification. CLD 11.3.1.
Quasi-smoothness is geometric regularity. For morphisms between good analytic spaces, smoothness is equivalent to quasi-smoothness together with relative interior. CLD 11.4.8–9.

For an analytic-domain inclusion, relative interior is ordinary topological interior. If f:Y→X has separated target, Int(Y/X)∩f⁻¹(Int(X))=Int(Y) and ∂Y=∂(Y/X)∪f⁻¹(∂X). Algebraic analytifications are boundaryless; boundaryless morphisms compose and remain boundaryless under analytic base change. CLD 11.4.1; Conrad–Temkin Lemma 2.9.

Finite analytic maps are boundaryless and proper, have affinoid inverse images of affinoid domains, and correspond on affinoids to finite Banach algebra maps. Finite ring A-algebras have their canonical finite-module Banach topology. If k is nontrivially valued and A is strict, a Banach A-algebra finite as a ring algebra has that finite Banach topology. CLD 11.4.3–4.

For an analytic morphism f:Y→X, dim_y f is the local dimension of the actual H(f(y))-analytic fibre and is Zariski upper semicontinuous. The map is finite at y exactly when dim_y f=0 and y lies in Int(Y/X); for good spaces this yields finite maps between affinoid neighbourhoods. Ducros Theorem 4.9, CLD 11.4.5, and Berkovich 3.1.4 and 3.1.10.

Over a complete nontrivially valued field K, every maximal ideal of a strict K-affinoid algebra has residue field finite over K, and its residue-field valuation defines a rigid analytic point. Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, 2.2, Corollaries 12–13.

A finite algebraic extension of a complete non-Archimedean valued field has a unique extending absolute value and is complete for it, without a separability hypothesis. Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, Appendix A, Theorem 3.

Over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field, every connected normal one-dimensional strict affinoid space is an affinoid domain of a nonsingular complete algebraic curve. Van der Put, Theorem 1.1.

A pure one-dimensional rig-smooth strict affinoid over a complete nontrivially valued field becomes, after a finite separable ground-field extension, isomorphic to an affinoid domain of a smooth proper algebraic curve. Thuillier, proof of Theorem 2.3.8.

Over a nontrivially valued field, the passage from Hausdorff strict Berkovich spaces to their rigid spaces is fully faithful, and rigid open affinoid domains correspond to strict Berkovich affinoid domains. In particular it preserves the affinoid algebra, morphism, and domain structure in the affinoid-to-algebraic-curve application. Berkovich 1.6.1–2.

On an algebraic variety over Wanner’s algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field, Wanner’s smooth forms on ordinary opens have algebraic tropical-chart presentations by regular unit moments. For a continuous function u, Wanner’s differentiated current acts by α↦∫u d′d′′α; psh means upper semicontinuity and positivity of that current. Wanner Definitions 3.11 and 3.15–16.

On algebraic analytifications, algebraic-unit tropical integration agrees with canonical analytic CLD integration, including its tropical multiplicities and lattice calibration. Canonical analytic calibration and integration are invariant under analytic isomorphisms and compatible with analytic-domain restriction. Gubler 5.20, 7.6 and 7.11; CLD 14.3.5 and 15.7.1–2.

Let K be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, C a smooth proper algebraic K-curve, W an ordinary open in Cᵃⁿ, and u:W→R continuous. If u is psh in Wanner’s positive-current sense, then u is Thuillier-subharmonic. Wanner Theorem 4.7.

For a pure one-dimensional rig-smooth strict affinoid Y over a complete nontrivially valued field, restriction of harmonic functions to its finite boundary induces H(Y)≅Hom(Γ(Y),R); thus each real boundary assignment has a unique harmonic extension. Thuillier Lemma 2.3.9.

On a smooth strict analytic curve over a nontrivially valued field, finite GR-subharmonicity agrees with Thuillier-subharmonicity, and a real-valued function is Thuillier-harmonic exactly when both signs are subharmonic. GR 3.4.2 and 3.12.
The finite normalization of a reduced strict analytic curve is rig-smooth over a perfect field and is an isomorphism outside a discrete rigid set. GR Lemma 3.9(1–2).

For continuous functions on separated pure analytic curves, GR harmonicity is a sheaf, is preserved and detected by every analytic field extension, and pulls back along every analytic curve morphism; it is also detected by a finite surjective curve morphism. No reducedness or separability hypothesis is required. GR Proposition 3.14(1,6,7).
On an analytic curve, classical psh in GR Definition 4.1, with every analytic extension and every analytic curve-map quantifier, is equivalent to GR-subharmonicity. GR 4.1.2.

On any strict analytic curve over a nontrivially valued field, including a nonreduced curve, a continuous function is GR-harmonic exactly when it is R-PL in the G-local analytic-unit convention and every residual line-bundle class is numerically trivial. For an R-PL function this numerical triviality is GJR harmonicity. GR Proposition 3.15; GJR Definition 7.2 and Remark 7.3(1).

Good Hausdorff analytic spaces are locally holomorphically and differentially separated.
